# AOSP header reference archive

Reference material only. Nothing in this directory is added to the AVOS build
include paths. Keep `../include/21` unchanged unless a separate compatibility
change is reviewed and tested.

## Scope

`snapshots/` contains all `.h`, `.hpp`, `.hxx` and `.inc` files under the explicit
header-family roots in `snapshots/INDEX.json`, plus graphics `.hal`/`.aidl`
interface definitions and license/notice files present in those archives.
It covers the old dump's graphics/window, HAL, media, Binder and utility families
and their newer locations. It is not a checkout of all AOSP repositories, a
complete Android build sysroot, or a dump of vendor implementations.

One immutable `android-<version>_r1` release tag is selected per API level 23–37:
Android 6.0, 7.0, 7.1, 8.0, 8.1, 9, 10, 11, 12, 12L, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17.
This does not cover every maintenance tag, minor SDK release, or development
branch. Each project is resolved to a commit before archiving; tags absent from
projects that did not exist yet are recorded explicitly.

Every `SNAPSHOT.json` records the project, release tag, resolved commit/tree,
archive URLs/checksums, per-file SHA-256 and size, and forwarding-link metadata.
Original header contents and license notices are preserved. Symlinks are recorded
rather than followed or created: some point outside the selected archive roots.
When AOSP has case-distinct filenames that cannot coexist on macOS, the second
file has an `.aosp-case-...` storage name. Its original `path` and actual
`stored_path` are both in the manifest; no file content is discarded.

## Version-control policy: lightweight audit tools

Commit only these tools and written conclusions:

- This README and `.gitignore`.
- `dump_aosp_headers.py`, `audit_layouts.py`, `audit_constants.py`,
  `audit_helpers.py`, `fetch_evidence.py` and `test_dump_aosp_headers.py`.
- `../../../doc/android_private_headers_audit.md`: manually written findings
  and limitations, which the scripts do not regenerate.
- The companion `../include/dump.sh` wrapper and `../include/README.md`.

Everything downloaded or generated stays local and is ignored by Git:

| Local artifact | Purpose and regeneration |
|---|---|
| `snapshots/`, including all manifests | Headers, interfaces and download provenance; generated by the downloader from the release tags configured in its source. |
| `baseline/` | The six comparison headers; recover from the recorded AVOS commit below. |
| `http-cache/` | Download cache; populated automatically. |
| `layouts/` | Extracted C declarations and ABI measurements; generated by `audit_layouts.py`. |
| `constants.json`, `helpers.json` | Comparison results; generated by the corresponding audit scripts. |
| `evidence/api-*/` and `evidence/INDEX.json` | Selected AOSP implementation sources and provenance; generated by `fetch_evidence.py`. |
| `evidence/avos/` | Copies of audited AVOS sources; recover from the recorded Git commit. |
| `inventory.json` | Optional totals from the original integrity check; not regenerated by the commands below or needed to rerun the audit. |

Keep existing local artifacts for future comparisons. Do not force-add them.
The report's links to generated artifacts are local evidence links, not files
provided in a fresh checkout. Most resolve after running the commands below;
the optional original inventory and AVOS evidence copies are not recreated.

A fresh checkout resolves the configured AOSP release tags again. This lightweight
commit does not preserve the original audit's per-file checksums or independently
pin the original AOSP revisions. Keep local manifests if that provenance matters.
When those manifests are available, the downloader restores missing files from
their recorded commits and checks archive and file hashes without re-resolving
tags. Existing differing files are rejected instead of overwritten. Missing
network access prevents downloading but does not affect the AVOS build.

## Reproduce or extend

Convenience entry point from the repository root:

```sh
./external/android/include/dump.sh --api 23 --jobs 2
```

Omit `--api` for all selected releases, or repeat it for several API levels.
The wrapper always downloads into this reference directory; it rejects the old
local-AOSP import arguments and does not accept an output-directory override.

Run from this directory (Python 3.9+):

```sh
# Recover the six-header baseline when it is absent (requires this Git history).
mkdir -p baseline
git -C ../../.. archive 1329243c7d0d5221ea2e578ad9f376cd6f6c5148 \
  external/android/include/21 | tar -xf - -C baseline --strip-components=4

python3 -m unittest test_dump_aosp_headers
python3 dump_aosp_headers.py --output snapshots --jobs 2
python3 audit_layouts.py --snapshots snapshots --baseline baseline \
  --ndk /opt/android-sdk/ndk/30.0.14904198 --output layouts
python3 audit_constants.py --snapshots snapshots --baseline baseline \
  --output constants.json
python3 audit_helpers.py --snapshots snapshots --baseline baseline \
  --output helpers.json
python3 fetch_evidence.py
```

These commands recreate the comparison results and selected AOSP evidence.
They do not regenerate the written audit report, the original inventory totals,
or the AVOS evidence copies. The audited AVOS revision is recorded in
`baseline/PROVENANCE.json`: `1329243c7d0d5221ea2e578ad9f376cd6f6c5148`
("Reset native-window rotation explicitly and report transform errors").
For example, recover an audited consumer from the repository root with:

```sh
git show 1329243c7d0d5221ea2e578ad9f376cd6f6c5148:external/android/libavos_android/android_buffer.c
```

The other copied AVOS inputs were
`external/android/libavos_android/android_window.c` and
`Include/android_config.h`; retrieve them at the same revision when needed.
The Git history containing that commit must be available locally.

The layout runner currently uses the macOS NDK host toolchain. It extracts the
original C record declarations and supplies forward declarations for unrelated
pointer types; it does not compile the entire AOSP header dependency graph.
No device code is executed by these scripts. ABI measurements do not establish
vendor/runtime behavior or validate an arbitrary native-window pointer.

The downloader rate-limits requests, retries transient errors and reuses checked
snapshots. Downloads are cached in ignored `http-cache/`. It refuses to replace
an existing snapshot file with different bytes. Use a new output directory for a
new snapshot policy. The `../include/dump.sh` wrapper fixes the output location
to this reference directory and cannot regenerate the production headers.
Adding release tags or archive roots requires updating the explicit downloader
configuration and reviewing the resulting manifests.
